panels.title: Currently-raised alerts (drops when a paired cleared arrives)
panels.description: Survivability alert view over the catalyst.alert.* Loki stream (service_name=catalyst.broker). Shows per (host_name,event_label) the NET raised-minus-cleared count over the last 20m; rows with net>0 are still raised. A row DROPS once its paired cleared event arrives (raised==cleared) or when raised heartbeats stop for 20m. Filters on host_name (the alert stream's field) — NOT catalyst_node_name / $node, which the alert stream does not carry, so this shows ALL raised alerts fleet-wide. KNOWN GAPS: (1) the spec payload {kind,reason,source,count,threshold,sinceMs} is NOT present in Loki — only event_label/host_name/severity_text/timestamp are shown. (2) No cleared event has ever been observed (4 raised / 0 cleared in 30d); the 20m window is the de-facto resolve. (3) Only needs_human_pileup observed live; system_down is built-for but unverified.

targets.expr: sum by (host_name, event_label, severity_text) (count_over_time({service_name=`catalyst.broker`} | event_entity=`alert` | event_action=`raised` [20m])) - (sum by (host_name, event_label, severity_text) (count_over_time({service_name=`catalyst.broker`} | event_entity=`alert` | event_action=`cleared` [20m])) or sum by (host_name, event_label, severity_text) (count_over_time({service_name=`catalyst.broker`} | event_entity=`alert` | event_action=`raised` [20m])) * 0)

panels.description:
**Control-loop wedge signals** — counts over the dashboard range. Each marks *the loop still running but doing no useful work*; on a healthy fleet most sit at **0**.

Each signal marks "loop still running, but no useful work happening":

- `holding new-work dispatch` (WARN) — The live worker-count snapshot (`claude agents --json`) is stale or empty, so the scheduler can't trust its in-flight count and admits **zero new tickets** this tick. The daemon looks alive (timers tick, in-flight phases advance) but no *new* work enters the pipeline. If the snapshot never recovers, the team starves with no crash.
- `reconcile failed` (ERROR) — A `registry.json` change fired a reconcile and it threw. The daemon keeps ticking on the **old** project set: newly registered projects are never picked up, de-registrations never take effect. No restart, no visible error besides this line.
- `liveness warmer: refresh failed` (WARN) — The short-interval timer that keeps the worker-count snapshot warm between ticks failed to refresh. This warmer is what *prevents* `holding new-work dispatch`; sustained failures make the snapshot go stale and cascade into it — the loop runs but goes blind on worker liveness.
- `stale fence` (WARN) — On a ≥2-host cluster, this node decided it is **no longer the current owner** of a ticket and **suppressed an outbound Linear/GitHub write** (zombie guard, fail-closed). A single event is the guard **working correctly**. A *sustained high rate* means an un-reaped zombie worker is stuck re-trying — see Fence terms below. Single-host installs never emit this.
- `tick failed` (ERROR) — An uncaught exception escaped the whole scheduler tick; the top-level catch logged it and scheduled the next tick. The daemon survives but **this entire tick did no work** (no advancement, no dispatch, no sweep). If it recurs every tick, the control loop is frozen while the process stays up.
- `registry has 0 projects` (WARN) — At boot the registry resolved to **zero** enrolled projects, so there is nothing to ever dispatch. The daemon looks perfectly healthy (PID present, timers armed) but every tick is a no-op. Usually a host that never ran `catalyst-execution-core register`. Emitted once at startup.
- `not in the cluster roster` (WARN) — This host's name is **absent from a ≥2-host roster**, so under HRW ownership-hashing every ticket routes to some *other* host and this daemon owns zero tickets — a silent self-eviction. Registry is fine; the *ownership partition* excludes this node. Single-host (`roster ≤ 1`) never emits this.

options.content:
## Wedge signals — what each one means

Each signal marks "loop still running, but no useful work happening":

- `holding new-work dispatch` (WARN) — The live worker-count snapshot (`claude agents --json`) is stale or empty, so the scheduler can't trust its in-flight count and admits **zero new tickets** this tick. The daemon looks alive (timers tick, in-flight phases advance) but no *new* work enters the pipeline. If the snapshot never recovers, the team starves with no crash.
- `reconcile failed` (ERROR) — A `registry.json` change fired a reconcile and it threw. The daemon keeps ticking on the **old** project set: newly registered projects are never picked up, de-registrations never take effect. No restart, no visible error besides this line.
- `liveness warmer: refresh failed` (WARN) — The short-interval timer that keeps the worker-count snapshot warm between ticks failed to refresh. This warmer is what *prevents* `holding new-work dispatch`; sustained failures make the snapshot go stale and cascade into it — the loop runs but goes blind on worker liveness.
- `stale fence` (WARN) — On a ≥2-host cluster, this node decided it is **no longer the current owner** of a ticket and **suppressed an outbound Linear/GitHub write** (zombie guard, fail-closed). A single event is the guard **working correctly**. A *sustained high rate* means an un-reaped zombie worker is stuck re-trying — see Fence terms below. Single-host installs never emit this.
- `tick failed` (ERROR) — An uncaught exception escaped the whole scheduler tick; the top-level catch logged it and scheduled the next tick. The daemon survives but **this entire tick did no work** (no advancement, no dispatch, no sweep). If it recurs every tick, the control loop is frozen while the process stays up.
- `registry has 0 projects` (WARN) — At boot the registry resolved to **zero** enrolled projects, so there is nothing to ever dispatch. The daemon looks perfectly healthy (PID present, timers armed) but every tick is a no-op. Usually a host that never ran `catalyst-execution-core register`. Emitted once at startup.
- `not in the cluster roster` (WARN) — This host's name is **absent from a ≥2-host roster**, so under HRW ownership-hashing every ticket routes to some *other* host and this daemon owns zero tickets — a silent self-eviction. Registry is fine; the *ownership partition* excludes this node. Single-host (`roster ≤ 1`) never emits this.

### Fence / zombie-guard terms

- **generation** — A monotonic integer ("fencing token") stamped on a ticket each time a host claims a phase. A fresh claim, revive, or cross-host takeover bumps it. The highest generation is, by definition, the current owner.
- **fence** — The check run *before* every external write that compares the generation a worker holds against the generation currently recorded on the ticket. Equal → still the owner, proceed. Not equal → bow out.
- **stale fence** — A worker's held generation is *lower* than the ticket's current generation: someone took over after this worker started. The fence fires, the write is rejected. The worker is a leftover from a superseded generation.
- **zombie guard** — The whole protective mechanism: a paused/partitioned worker that wakes *after* another host took its ticket is structurally prevented from corrupting shared Linear/GitHub state, because its stale generation no longer matches.
- **fail-closed** — When the fence can't be *affirmatively* confirmed current (missing signal/claim, spawn error, timeout, unparseable output), the answer defaults to "not current" and the write is suppressed. Only an explicit confirmation permits a write.
- **A single stale fence is healthy; a high rate is the alarm.** The fence only suppresses the *write*, not the process. If the underlying worker is never reaped it keeps waking, re-hitting the write site, and re-failing — burning ticks forever. A sustained high `stale fence` rate is therefore an alarm for the **reaper layer** (the phantom-reaper problem), not the fence layer.
